Would you step into the cage? Comment YES or NO.

caption:
This Sunday your clock moves back 1 hour. Your body's clock doesn't. ⏰

Hour 0: the master clock in your brain still runs on the old time
Day 1: hunger, sleep and energy hit at the wrong time
Day 2-3: morning light starts resetting you
About a week: your body clock catches up

And the twist is in your heart.

Save this for Sunday. Keep the clock change or end it? Comment below.

Source: Janszky & Ljung, New England Journal of Medicine, 2008 (Karolinska Institutet); circadian rhythm basics.

#nexthuman #clockchange #circadianrhythm #bodyclock #health
first_comment: Fun fact: the risky one is the SPRING change, when we lose an hour. Next up: how many steps your brain really needs 🚶

caption:
Forget 10,000 steps. Your brain may start thanking you at 3,000. 🧠🚶

0 steps: a toxic protein, tau, builds up faster
3,000-5,000 a day: memory decline came about 3 years later
5,000-7,500 a day: about 7 years later
10,000? The benefit leveled off way before that

Save this and check your step counter tonight.
How many steps did you do today?

Source: Harvard Aging Brain Study, Nature Medicine, Nov 2025 (Mass General Brigham).

#nexthuman #alzheimers #brainhealth #walking #longevity
first_comment: Honest note: this study shows a link, not proof that walking prevents Alzheimer's. Talk to your doctor before big changes. Next up: why astronauts come back taller 🚀

caption:
Astronauts come back from space taller. Here's what space does to your body. 🚀

Day 0: gravity lets go of you
Day 1: fluids rush to your head, your face gets puffy
Day 2: your legs get thinner ("bird legs")
Weeks: your spine discs expand, you grow taller
Landing: gravity takes it all back

Would you go to space to grow taller? YES or NO.
Save this.

Source: NASA; reports on NASA astronaut Scott Kelly after his year in space.

#nexthuman #space #astronaut #nasa #humanbody
first_comment: Bad news: the height goes away once gravity is back. Next up: the 2 threats scientists say could wipe out humanity ⚠️

caption:
Scientists just listed the threats that could end humanity. Only two could wipe us out. ⚠️

17 threats to our health, from now to 2100:
Superbugs that no antibiotic can kill
Toxic air and a heating planet
Nuclear war and the famine after it
AI in the wrong hands

The odds are low. The stakes are everything.

Which one scares you most? Comment.

Source: The Lancet Commission on 21st-century global threats to health, October 2026.

caption:
Your strongest muscle isn't your biceps. And it's not your tongue either. 💪

It depends how you measure:
Force: your jaw closes your teeth with about 200 pounds
Work: your heart never stops
Size: your glutes are the biggest
Record bite: 975 pounds, for 2 seconds

Send this to the friend who only trains biceps.

Source: Library of Congress, Everyday Mysteries; Scientific American, "Fact or Fiction: The Tongue Is the Strongest Muscle"; Guinness World Records (1986).

caption:
Stop putting cotton swabs in your ears. 👂

They push the wax deeper, toward your eardrum.
In the US, about 34 kids a day went to the ER with cotton swab ear injuries (1990-2010).
Your ears clean themselves: chewing and talking move old wax out on its own.

Send this to the friend who swabs every morning.

Source: Nationwide Children's Hospital, The Journal of Pediatrics 2017; American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, earwax guideline 2017.

#nexthuman #earwax #ears #health #science

caption:
Your cut heals. But only to about 80% of its old strength. 🩹

Minutes: platelets plug it, a clot seals it
Days 1-3: white blood cells eat the bacteria
Up to week 3: new tissue fills the gap
Up to 2 years: the scar keeps getting stronger, but stops around 80%

Send this to the friend who picks at scabs.

Source: wound healing physiology (hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, remodeling), Physiopedia; Cleveland Clinic Laboratories.

#nexthuman #woundhealing #skin #bodyfacts #science
first_comment: Timings change with the size and depth of the cut. Deep or dirty wound? Get it checked. Next: the squeeze test your bones win against concrete 🦴

caption:
Your bones are stronger than concrete. 🦴

Squeeze test:
House concrete cracks at about 20-30 MPa
Bone tissue holds about 200 MPa
That's around 6x more

But hit a bone from the side and it breaks much easier: bone is strongest when squeezed along its length.
And unlike concrete, bone is alive. It repairs itself.

Send this to the friend who thinks they're made of glass.

Source: Reilly & Burstein, Journal of Biomechanics 1975 (human cortical bone); standard strength of residential concrete.

#nexthuman #bones #anatomy #bodyfacts #science
first_comment: Compression only: in bending and twisting bone is much weaker. Next: the surgery that breaks your legs on purpose 🦵

caption:
Doctors can break your legs to make you taller. 🦵

Day 0: surgeons cut the bone on purpose
Then: a device pulls it apart, about 1 mm a day
New bone fills the gap: about 1 inch a month
The price: about $100,000 at one US hospital, plus months of rehab

Complications are common. It's major surgery, not a shortcut.

Would you do it? Send this to the friend who wants to be taller.

Source: Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS); Penn Medicine limb lengthening program; Hong Kong Medical Journal.

#nexthuman #height #surgery #limblengthening #science
first_comment: Not a recommendation: it's elective surgery with real risks. Next: you fall into ice water. The first minute decides 🧊

caption:
You fall into ice water. The first minute decides. 🧊

The 1-10-1 rule:
1 minute: cold shock. You gasp and hyperventilate. Control your breathing.
10 minutes: of useful movement before your arms stop working
1 hour: before hypothermia knocks you out

Most cold-water deaths happen before hypothermia. So don't panic-swim: float, slow your breathing, then get out.

Send this to the friend who swims in winter.

Source: Prof. Gordon Giesbrecht, University of Manitoba (1-10-1 principle).

#nexthuman #coldwater #survival #icewater #science
first_comment: The times are rough: they change with water temperature, body size and clothing. A life jacket keeps your head up. Heart condition? Talk to your doctor before cold plunges.
